title: Basic Fluid Pressure
description: Explore how normal force and contact area determine pressure in a bounded introductory model.

firstScreen.purpose: Change normal force or contact area and see the calculated pressure respond.

inputs.label: Normal force
inputs.validation: Reject non-finite values and constrain values to the educational interaction range.
inputs.educationalDescription: The magnitude of force acting normally on the surface.

inputs.label: Contact area
inputs.validation: Reject non-finite or zero values and constrain values to the educational interaction range.
inputs.educationalDescription: The surface area over which the normal force is distributed.

outputs.label: Calculated pressure
outputs.interpretation: A larger force or a smaller area produces a larger pressure in this model.

learningOutcomes: Describe pressure as normal force distributed over an area.
Identify the SI units Pa, N, and m^2 and predict how force or area changes pressure.
Calculate and interpret pressure from force and area within the stated model limits.

blocks.text: This visual foundation introduces pressure as the magnitude of normal force divided by the area over which it acts.
Estimated completion time: 25 minutes, including approximately 10 minutes of interaction.
Use basic division and recognise newtons and square metres before starting.
LO-FP-001: describe pressure; LO-FP-002: identify units and predict changes; LO-FP-003: calculate and interpret a pressure result.
The relationship helps engineers reason about how a normal force is distributed across a contact surface before later lessons introduce complete fluid-power systems.

blocks.definition: The magnitude of normal force divided by the area over which it acts in this introductory model.

blocks.title: Normal force distributed over contact area
blocks.altText: A downward normal force arrow acts on a rectangular contact surface; labels report force, area, and calculated pressure.
blocks.description: The force arrow and contact surface are representational. Their documented visual scales do not represent physical distance.
blocks.caption: Original Industrial Learn pressure concept diagram.

blocks.text: Pressure describes how normal force is distributed over an area. The same force produces greater pressure when it acts over a smaller area.
The force acts normally over the stated area, inputs are consistent SI values, and the result is not an equipment rating or complete design conclusion.

blocks.name: Pressure from normal force and area

blocks.note: One pascal is one newton per square metre. Industrial Learn supplies force in N and area in m^2 to the calculation.

blocks.title: Pressure from a known force and area

steps.label: Check units
steps.expression: F in N, A in m^2
steps.explanation: Both quantities are in the SI units expected by the governing calculation.

steps.label: Calculate pressure
steps.explanation: The pressure is 100,000 pascals, displayed as 100 kilopascals.

blocks.interpretation: This result applies only to the stated force-over-area educational model.

blocks.text: The first-screen visual changes normal force and contact area, while engineering-core supplies the pressure result. It has no time progression or fault state.
Fault diagnosis is outside this foundational lesson and is introduced only after measurement systems and supported fault models are taught.
This educational calculation does not provide equipment operating instructions, component ratings, or professional design approval.

blocks.prompt: For the same normal force, what happens when the contact area becomes smaller?
blocks.answerExplanation: Because p = F / A, reducing area while keeping force fixed increases pressure.

blocks.text: Pressure is normal force per unit area. Increase force at fixed area to increase pressure; decrease area at fixed force to increase pressure.

blocks.note: Introduction to Pressure in Fluid Mechanics.

blocks.text: Continue to pressure measurement and hydraulic applications after those lessons complete source and engineering review.

blocks.title: Units, rearrangement, and model limits
blocks.description: Optional detail preserves SI reasoning and excluded physical effects.
blocks.content: Pressure is defined as normal force per area: p = F/A. Algebraically, this can be rearranged to F = pA when pressure and area are known. Since 1 Pa = 1 N/m^2, dividing newtons by square metres produces pascals. This visual calculates only the force-area relationship. It does not calculate flow, leakage, compressibility, losses, transients, component ratings, or structural capacity.
